explanation: A singer holds a low drone while shaping the mouth and throat to bring out a whistling melody above it. Neighbouring Tuva, a republic of Russia, has a closely related tradition.

claims.text: Khöömei throat singing is a traditional art of Mongolia.
Khöömei is not a tradition of Nepal, Japan or Thailand.
In khöömei a single singer produces two pitches at once: a low drone and a melody of overtones.
Tuva, a republic of Russia that borders Mongolia, has a closely related throat-singing tradition.
